newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy police crack Europe-wide silver scam.
newsitem.headline: Italy police crack Europe-wide silver scam.

text.p: Italian tax police said on Monday they had cracked a massive Europe-wide silver trafficking racket, seizing over 20 tonnes of silver, and had arrested six men.

"Operation Foil", directed by Milan tax police with the help of police forces in Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands, had discovered a vast network importing silver into Italy from Swiss banks avoiding the payment of value-added tax.

Milan tax police said in a statement that with the help of the European Commission's anti-fraud division they had uncovered a network of 23 Italian and foreign shell companies as well as individuals acting as a front for the import of the silver.

Police said the network had avoided paying tax of some 120 billion lire ($80 million) in Italy and around 24 million marks ($36 million) in Germany "thanks to the trafficking of the precious metal through a merry-go-round of phantom or filter companies."

The statement said the silver was sold by the organisers of the racket, backed by companies operating in Switzerland, to firms in Italy and throughout the European Union and then the fake Italian companies were invoiced for the subsequent sale.

"In this way the criminals achieved their fraudulent aim of making the Swiss silver appear as if it had originated in the EU, so avoiding paying the tax due on imports from Switzerland," the police said.
In Italy, the front companies then sold the silver to Italian silversmiths at a price below that quoted on the official London market, routing their profits to Swiss bank accounts.
The Milan tax police said the 20 tonnes of silver had been seized in Italy. Investigations related to money laundering were continuing.
